newsitem.title: USA: Conn. atty genl urges $33 mln in power credits.
newsitem.headline: Conn. atty genl urges $33 mln in power credits.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal said Friday that customers of Connecticut Light & Power, a subsidiary of troubled Northeast Utilities, should get credits on their bills worth $33 million because they cannot count on reliable electric service.
Blumenthal urged the state Department of Public Utility Control (DPUC) to order a one-time, 25 percent credit for all customers.
He said this was necessary because the threat of brownouts and blackouts during summer has reduced the quality of service for Connecticut Light & Power (CL&P) customers.
Blumenthal also said the DPUC should order additional credits of up to 20 percent if the lights dim or go out in any month this summer.

"CL&P customers are paying too much for electric service that they can no longer rely on," Blumenthal said in a statement. "These rates were not granted with the expectation that, at any time, residential and business customers might face brownouts or blackouts."

Northeast Utilities' three Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn., have been shut down since March 1996 because of safety problems. The utility has said it intends to have all three plants ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by federal regulators.
Connecticut's electricity rates are among the highest in the U.S. A controversial bid to deregulate the state's electricity industry was put on hold this year when the state Senate dropped the bill.
Blumenthal has said that Connecticut's failure to move swiftly on deregulation could hurt the state's economic competitiveness.

"Customers should be compensated for the uncertainty created by the mismanagement of these nuclear plants and all customers should receive credits in each month when brownouts and blackouts occur," Blumenthal said.
His proposal to the DPUC calls for a one-time credit of $25, or 25 percent, whichever is greater, based on customers' July usage.
This would amount to about $33 million in customer credits, he said.
In addition, Blumenthal said all CL&P customers should receive a $10, or 15 percent credit, whichever is greater, in any month there is one day of brownouts or blackouts.
They should receive a $15, or 20 percent credit, whichever is greater, in any month where there are two days of brownouts or blackouts, Blumenthal said.
